2) Target budget range for the initial 6–12 months (ARR or monthly committed spend).

4) Preferred marketplace(s) for purchase (AWS, GCP, Azure) and whether you require a private offer through the marketplace or direct invoice via Redwood Private/Dedicated.

If you can reply with ballpark numbers we'll produce a short spreadsheet that maps Redwood list/unit prices to expected marketplace unit prices (inc. estimated marketplace fees/commissions) and recommend the best PO path.

I attached a short MAP (mutual action plan) and will follow up with Rafael to draft the price mapping once we have volumes.

Next steps: please reply with 1–4 above by EOD Thu so we can get pricing to your procurement team before next week's steering committee.

Hi all —

Thanks for the volume & budget ranges. I cranked a quick mapping with conservative marketplace take rates and internal discounts. High-level assumptions used (feel free to push back):
- Redwood list: our hosted unit price (per 1M tokens) for the model class we demoed.
- AWS Marketplace fee: ~12% (includes AWS transaction fee + marketplace listing/reseller margin).
- Private offer allowance: customers can receive a discounted private-offer unit price vs. Redwood list, typically 10–30% depending on commit level.
- Target buckets: 50M / 150M / 300M tokens.

Suggested mapping (rounded):
- Redwood list $/1M tokens: 1) $1,800  2) $1,500  3) $1,200
- Private-offer negotiated discount (for BrightCart given commit): 20% at 50M, 25% at 150M, 30% at 300M
- Post-discount price per 1M: 1) $1,440  2) $1,125  3) $840
- Estimated AWS marketplace unit (adds 12% marketplace fee on top of Redwood net price): 1) $1,612  2) $1,260  3) $940

Notes:
- If procurement requires the marketplace to be the billed entity, the PO will reflect the marketplace unit price (final invoice reconciliation may vary depending on AWS Marketplace terms).
- For GCP/Azure we typically see slightly different fee structures (GCP ~10–12%, Azure ~13–15%); we can produce a comparative sheet.
- If BrightCart prefers to keep a fixed $/1M target (e.g., target $1,000/1M), we can run reverse math to show required commit / annual spend to hit that net price.

I attached a quick spreadsheet (AWS-focused) and a short note with the assumptions. Happy to refine once procurement confirms whether AWS private offers must be the checkout path (vs. Redwoods invoice + internal PO).

Cheers,
